questions.q: Which role is automatically available to every user in a Snowflake account, with no explicit grant required?
options: SYSADMIN
PUBLIC
SECURITYADMIN
ACCOUNTADMIN
questions.explain: PUBLIC is the implicit base of the role hierarchy — every user has it automatically, no grant needed.

questions.q: Per this lesson, why should custom roles typically be granted underneath SYSADMIN rather than ACCOUNTADMIN?
options: SYSADMIN is deprecated and should be avoided
So that SYSADMIN, not ACCOUNTADMIN, ends up owning the bulk of an account's day-to-day objects, keeping ACCOUNTADMIN membership minimal
Because ACCOUNTADMIN cannot grant roles
There is no difference between the two roles
questions.explain: ACCOUNTADMIN should be reserved for a tiny handful of people; SYSADMIN is the role most custom roles and day-to-day objects should sit under.

questions.q: What does it mean that SECURITYADMIN and SYSADMIN are granted to ACCOUNTADMIN in the role hierarchy graph?
options: ACCOUNTADMIN inherits everything SECURITYADMIN and SYSADMIN can do, without needing its own separate grants
ACCOUNTADMIN loses its own privileges once those roles are granted to it
SECURITYADMIN and SYSADMIN can no longer be used independently
It has no functional effect — it's purely visual in the graph
questions.explain: A role granted to another role inherits everything that role can do — that's why ACCOUNTADMIN, sitting above SECURITYADMIN and SYSADMIN, implicitly has their privileges too.

questions.q: Which system role is responsible for creating and managing users and roles, separate from granting privileges on data objects?
options: USERADMIN
ORGADMIN
PUBLIC
SYSADMIN
questions.explain: USERADMIN creates/manages users and roles; SECURITYADMIN is the one that manages grants — a deliberate separation of duties.

questions.q: What is the fastest way to confirm which role your current Snowsight session is using, per this lesson?
options: Run SHOW ROLES and read the first row
Check the role badge on a worksheet or open the Switch Role panel in the user menu
There is no way to check this in Snowsight
Ask an ACCOUNTADMIN to check for you
questions.explain: The worksheet role badge and the Switch Role panel both show your session's current active role directly in the UI.
